## EUROPE AND CENTRAL ASIA — profile (page 115)

- Header facts: region: Europe and Central Asia; coverage: 18 countries; income group: not shown; lending category: not shown; data status: not shown; population: 253 million; GNI: 2,763; unit line: US$ billion, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock 2025: 1,340, up +15.3% from 2024.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25: 854 in 2015 and 1,340 in 2025. The line rises overall from 2015 to 2025, with a small increase early on, a slight dip around ≈2017–18, then a steady climb through the early 2020s and a sharp jump to its peak in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 1,340
  - Public & publicly guaranteed: 588
  - Private nonguaranteed: 493
  - Short-term: 259
  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:
    - Multilateral: 254
    - Bilateral: 67
    - Private creditors: 267
  - Multilateral:
    - European Union: 84
    - World Bank-IBRD: 50
    - Other multilateral: 120
  - Bilateral:
    - China: 18
    - Russian Federation: 9
    - Other bilateral: 40

- Figure 3 Debt ratios:
  - External debt / exports: 152%, +10.7%. Trend: fluctuates, with a mid-period spike, then declines and edges back up by 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 49%, +0.3%. Trend: rises into the middle of the period, then trends downward toward 2025.
  - Debt service / exports: 25%, +8.1%. Trend: generally declines early, spikes around the middle-late period, drops, then rises again by 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 8%, -2.1%. Trend: broadly downward, with some fluctuation and a mild bump mid-period before falling again.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors:
    - Maturity: 29 yrs
    - Grace period: 7 yrs
    - Interest rate: 1.9%
  - Private creditors:
    - Maturity: 7 yrs
    - Grace period: 5 yrs
    - Interest rate: 5.3%

- Notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of Europe and Central Asia DRS reporting countries.
- Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
